children: State-ownedPower Grid Corporation of India Ltd (POWERGRID) on Monday (November 16) approved an investment of ₹220.09 crore for the reconductoring of the Gooty-Tumkur (Pavagada) 400-kilovolt (kV) double-circuit transmission line using a High Temperature Low Sag (HTLS) conductor.

The investment approval was granted by the company's Committee of Directors on Investment on Projects at a meeting held on November 16, 2026. The project is scheduled to be commissioned by June 10, 2028.

Last week, Power Grid Corporation of India said it has been declared the successful bidder for an intra-state transmission project in Karnataka, with quoted annual transmission charges of ₹243.34 crore.

The project, awarded under the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) process, involves setting up a 3X500 MVA, 400/220 kV substation at Humnabad in Bidar district and associated transmission lines. It will be developed on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) basis.

Power Grid Corporation received the Letter of Intent (LoI), dated November 10, on November 11, 2026. The project includes establishing a new 400/220 kV substation at Humnabad, along with the construction of 400 kV and 220 kV transmission lines across Karnataka and associated bays.

With this win, Power Grid Corporation has secured 11 transmission system projects under the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding route in FY27 so far. The cumulative annual transmission charges for these projects stand at ₹8,106.97 crore.
Shares of Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd ended at ₹262.00, up by ₹4.35, or 1.69%, on the BSE.

title: Power Grid approves ₹220 crore investment for 400 kV transmission line reconductoring project
